problem_statement: ashutosh1919/masterPortfolio is a runnable Create-React-App software-developer portfolio built on a shared design system: a React-Router (BrowserRouter) shell in src/containers/Main.js registers every route (/home, /education, /experience, /projects, /opensource, /contact, /resume), a shared src/components/header/Header.js renders the site-wide top navigation as a <ul class=menu> of react-router NavLinks, a shared src/components/footer/Footer.js renders the credit strip, and product sections (for example src/pages/projects and src/components/githubRepoCard) are built from a reusable highlight-tinted card pattern (a title, a subtitle, a description paragraph, and a footer detail row) laid out in a flex-wrap card grid. The portfolio has an About greeting, Education, Experience, Projects and Open Source pages, but it has NO page that collects the concrete, measurable outcomes of the work into one place. Add a new cross-page 'Impact Case Studies' section at the /impact route that is a first-class member of the existing design system: it must reuse the shared Header and Footer chrome, present at least six case studies rendered from the shared card pattern (each an <h3> title with a client label, a description, and a measured outcome), and be registered in the shared navigation so an 'Impact' nav link appears on the top menu of both the Home page and the new Impact page. Because the grid holds several disciplines, give the page its own 'Focus by discipline' filter that belongs to the grid itself: a row of chips (All / Performance / Product / Platform, each showing how many case studies it holds) sitting above the cards, wired so selecting a chip filters the case-study grid to that discipline AND updates a live count readout line (for example 'Showing 2 of 6 · Performance'). To keep the focus control consistent across the product surfaces that carry outcome cards, render the same 'Focus by discipline' filter on the Projects page too. The new page must be reachable via the shared router, consistent with the portfolio's typography, palette and card rhythm; the discipline filter's chip row must wrap without horizontal overflow at mobile and tablet widths; the filtered case-study grid must keep the shared card layout intact (cards must not collapse or overlap into an unreadable pile); the count readout must stay in sync with the selected chip after a click; and the change must not introduce console/network errors or horizontal overflow at desktop, tablet or mobile widths. Do not build a bespoke standalone page bolted on beside the design system, do not leave the route unregistered so it falls through to the 404 page, do not collapse the case-study grid into an illegible overlapping stack, and do not leave the discipline filter's count readout frozen when a chip is selected.
required_content: A new Impact Case Studies page renders at the /impact route with a page heading 'Impact Case Studies' (an <h1>) and a short introductory sentence describing the section.
The page presents at least six case studies, each rendered from the shared card pattern with an <h3> case-study title, a client/context label, a description paragraph and a measured outcome metric.
The new page reuses the shared Header navigation and shared Footer chrome so it is visually and structurally consistent with the existing Home, Projects and Open Source pages.

The shared top navigation registers an 'Impact' link (an anchor carrying the nav-link class) that appears on the Home page menu AND on the new Impact page menu, so the section is reachable cross-page.
The /impact route is registered in the shared router (src/containers/Main.js) and resolves to the real Impact Case Studies page rather than falling through to the catch-all 404 page.

The Impact page carries its own 'Focus by discipline' filter (a section with the discipline-filter class): a chip row (All / Performance / Product / Platform with per-discipline counts) above the case-study grid, and the same filter is mirrored onto the Projects page so the focus control is consistent across surfaces.

The discipline filter filters the case-study grid AND keeps a live count readout in sync: clicking the 'Performance' chip filters the grid to the Performance case studies and updates the readout to read 'Showing 2 of 6 · Performance' rather than leaving it frozen at the default.

Desktop, tablet (834px) and mobile (390px) renderings of the new page and its discipline-filter chip row have no horizontal overflow, the filtered card grid stays legible (no collapsed/overlapping cards), and the page emits no console or network errors.
design_constraints: Preserve the portfolio's design system: the shared Header <ul class=menu> navigation, the shared Footer credit strip, the highlight-tinted card visual language (title + subtitle + description + footer detail row), the Google Sans typography, and the theme palette from src/theme.js.

Build the new section and its discipline filter from the existing reusable, highlight-tinted visual language (mirroring src/components/githubRepoCard and the flex-wrap card grid in src/pages/projects), not from a bespoke off-system layout with inline hard-coded colours.

Register the new page inside the shared React-Router registry in src/containers/Main.js and the shared navigation in src/components/header/Header.js, so routing and navigation stay centralised rather than duplicated.
The Impact nav link must carry the nav-link class and be part of the same shared menu as Home/Education/Experience/Projects, appearing consistently on every page that renders the Header.

Keep the new page and the discipline-filter chip row responsive: the case-study card grid and the chip row must wrap without horizontal overflow at 390px mobile and 834px tablet widths, matching the existing responsive breakpoints.

Keep the filtered case-study grid intact: filtering must re-render the shared cards in the normal flex-wrap rhythm, never with negative margins or overlap that collapse the cards into an unreadable pile.
Keep the discipline filter's count readout reactive: it must recompute from the currently selected discipline so the readout text tracks the active chip rather than a value cached once at setup.
Do not add remote fonts, analytics, ad or CDN scripts; the page must render offline with zero console and network errors.
state_constraints: desktop_home captures the current shared top navigation (Home/Education/Experience/Projects/Open Source/Contact Me) on the greeting page; after the change it also carries the new 'Impact' nav link so the section is reachable cross-page.
mobile_home captures the Home page at 390px, where the shared navigation stays intact with no horizontal overflow.

desktop_impact_route captures the /impact route: on the reference it renders the Impact Case Studies page (heading, intro, six shared cards in a clean flex-wrap grid, shared Header/Footer, and the page's 'Focus by discipline' filter above the grid); before the change the unregistered route falls through to the shared 404 page ('Woops' / '404').

desktop_impact_filter captures the /impact route after clicking the 'Focus by discipline' Performance chip: on the reference the grid filters to the Performance case studies and the count readout updates to 'Showing 2 of 6 · Performance'; a frozen readout that ignores the click is a regression.
mobile_impact_route captures the /impact route at 390px, where the case-study card grid and the discipline-filter chip row must wrap with no horizontal overflow.
tablet_impact_route captures the /impact route at 834px, where the card grid wraps to a multi-column layout with no horizontal overflow.

desktop_projects captures the existing Projects page, which must also carry the shared 'Focus by discipline' filter so the focus control stays consistent across the product surfaces that show outcome cards.

change_completion: The /impact route renders a real Impact Case Studies page with the 'Impact Case Studies' heading (an h1) and a short intro sentence.
The page presents at least six case-study cards, each with an h3 title, a client label, a description and a measured outcome metric.
design_consistency: The new page reuses the shared Header/Footer chrome and the highlight-tinted card pattern, and the shared navigation carries an Impact nav-link that appears on both Home and Impact.

The page's 'Focus by discipline' filter is built from the theme palette and the shared card language, and the same filter is mirrored onto the Projects page so the focus control is consistent cross-page.
regression: The existing shared navigation (Home/Education/Experience/Projects/Open Source/Contact Me) and the existing pages remain reachable and unchanged.
The discipline filter keeps its count readout in sync after a click and re-renders the filtered case-study grid in the normal card rhythm (no collapsed or overlapping cards).
responsive: Desktop, tablet (834px) and mobile (390px) renderings of the new page and the discipline-filter chip row have no horizontal overflow.
The case-study grid and the chip row wrap responsively at mobile and tablet widths and emit no console or network errors.
